complaint.product: Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan
complaint.narrative: I set up autopay for this loan six months ago and it worked fine until last month, when my payment was never withdrawn and I was charged a late fee as a result. I have a screenshot of my autopay settings still showing as active.

allegations: Autopay payment was never withdrawn last month
Charged a late fee as a result of the missed withdrawal
Autopay settings still show as active
extraction.account_details_mentioned: Autopay was set up six months ago and worked fine until last month; customer has a screenshot showing autopay settings as active

account.account_note: Installment loan, current. Opened 2025-10-27. Payments due on the 27th.

transactions.note: Autopay disabled by customer via mobile app
Scheduled installment $100.00 not received; no autopay instruction active

verification.fact_verification_explanation: Both problem events happened, but the records contradict the customer's explanation that the company failed to withdraw a payment it was supposed to. (1) Missed withdrawal: no payment was received on the 2026-05-27 due date. The log shows 'Scheduled installment $100.00 not received; no autopay instruction active.' (2) Late fee: a $25.00 late fee was assessed on 2026-06-01, following the missed payment. The cause was not a system failure. On 2026-05-09 the log shows 'Autopay disabled by customer via mobile app,' 18 days before the due date. Autopay had worked on 2026-03-27 and 2026-04-27 ($100.00 each), which matches the customer's account of it working until last month. The customer is right that the payment was not withdrawn and a late fee was charged. They are wrong that this was an error, because autopay had been turned off from their own account. The claim that autopay settings still show as active conflicts with the 2026-05-09 disable record. The screenshot is not on file, but the records directly contradict the allegation, so its absence does not change the verdict.
verification.risk_rationale: The amount is $25 with no attorney/regulator reference, fraud or identity dispute, misleading-terms allegation, hardship or vulnerability indicators, or embedded instructions, and the claim is confirmed false against clear records.

policy.topic: Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority
policy.text:
# Internal Policy: Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority

**Applies to:** Complaints where account/transaction data confirms a fee was charged in error, or where a goodwill gesture is being considered for a confirmed service failure.

## Authority thresholds
| Fee/credit amount | Who may approve |
|---|---|
| $0 – $50 | Complaints analyst, no additional sign-off required |
| $50.01 – $200 | Complaints analyst with supervisor co-sign |
| $200.01+ | Supervisor or manager approval required; analyst may not approve independently |

## When a waiver is appropriate
- The transaction history **confirms** the fee was charged in error (e.g., payment was received before the due date but a late fee was still assessed).
- The fee was charged due to a documented system or processing error.
- A documented goodwill exception for a first-time, low-dollar fee on an otherwise good-standing account (use sparingly, document the rationale).

## When a waiver is NOT appropriate
- The transaction history confirms the fee was correctly charged (no error occurred) — the response should explain the charge, not waive it.
- The complaint's underlying fact could not be verified (missing/incomplete data) — route to manual review rather than waiving preemptively.
- The complaint involves a dispute of right vs. convenience (e.g., customer disagrees with a disclosed, legitimate fee) — explain the fee and its basis; do not waive solely to end the complaint.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state the exact dollar amount being waived and the specific reason (tied to the confirmed error).
- May NOT waive a fee "as a one-time courtesy" without a documented rationale on file — every waiver must cite either a confirmed error or an explicit goodwill justification.

## Documentation requirement
Every waiver, regardless of amount, must be logged with: the confirming evidence (which transaction record), the dollar amount, and the approving party.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

draft.draft_text:
Thank you for writing to us about your autopay. You told us it was set up six months ago and worked fine until last month, when your payment wasn't taken out and you were charged a late fee. You also told us your autopay settings still show as active, and that you have a screenshot. We understand how frustrating it is to be charged a fee when you expected autopay to take care of your payment.

Here is what we found on each point.

The missed payment: You're right that the payment didn't come out. Our records show your $100.00 payment due May 27 was not received. Autopay did work for your payments on March 27 and April 27, $100.00 each time, which matches what you described.

The autopay setting: Our records show autopay was turned off through the mobile app on your account on May 9, which was 18 days before the May 27 due date. On May 27, the account had no active autopay instruction. That doesn't match what your screenshot shows, and we don't have the screenshot on file.

The late fee: A $25.00 late fee was charged on June 1, after the May 27 payment wasn't received. We didn't find an error in how this fee was charged, so we haven't removed it.

If you'd like us to look again, please send us your screenshot, along with the date it was taken if you know it. You're also welcome to send anything else you think we should see, at any time, and we'll review it. You can reply to this message or call us at the number on your account.

Case reference: 22853918
draft.policy_cited: 06 Fee Waiver and Goodwill Credit Authority, 'When a waiver is NOT appropriate' (transaction history confirms the fee was correctly charged; explain the charge rather than waive it). Also governed by Policy 10 (Prohibited Language) and Policy 11 (Response Tone and Format).
allegations_addressed: Autopay payment was never withdrawn last month
Charged a late fee as a result of the missed withdrawal
Autopay settings still show as active

verifier.completeness_check: pass — all three allegations are addressed individually: (1) the payment not withdrawn ("The missed payment" paragraph), (2) the late fee ("The late fee" paragraph), and (3) autopay still showing as active ("The autopay setting" paragraph).
verifier.groundedness_check: pass — The dates and amounts trace to the verification output: $100.00 due May 27 and not received, autopay disabled via the mobile app on May 9 (18 days earlier, which is correct), successful $100.00 autopay payments on March 27 and April 27, and a $25.00 late fee on June 1. The draft states no unsupported fact, date, or amount. 'Set up six months ago' and the screenshot are attributed to the customer ('You told us'). Minor note: 'That doesn't match what your screenshot shows' describes an unseen document. It reads as the customer's own account of the screenshot, and the draft states that the screenshot is not on file, so this is not a failure. The reviewer may want to soften it to 'what you described'.
verifier.policy_authorization_check: pass — The draft states no remedy and no waiver, and remedy_stated and referral_stated are both null. This is consistent with Policy 06, which says a fee confirmed as correctly charged should be explained, not waived. No authority threshold is implicated.
verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — No fault admission beyond confirmed fact: 'You're right that the payment didn't come out' is a verified fact, and the draft does not apologize or assign blame. No future guarantees, legal conclusions, or promises outside documented authority. Nothing discourages other channels; 'You're also welcome to send anything else... at any time' invites further input.
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — The draft follows Policy 11: an opening acknowledgment that references the specific complaint, findings with specific dates and amounts, an outcome (no error found, so the late fee is not removed), next steps (send the screenshot and date, reply or call), and the case reference number. It uses second person and plain language, with no marketing content. Each allegation gets its own short paragraph, and the length is acceptable for a multi-allegation response. Minor note: the outcome sits inside the late fee paragraph rather than in a separate paragraph, which is acceptable.
